path.name: Your First Affiliate Commission
path.tagline: Publish honest, helpful content about products you know and earn commission when readers buy through your links.
path.description: You pick a niche where people already buy things, choose one platform and join a few affiliate programs. Over 30 days you research what buyers search for before they purchase, publish honest reviews, comparisons and how-tos with clearly disclosed links, and track which posts get clicks. Commissions are usually small and slow at first, so the goal is a steady publishing habit, trust with your readers and possibly a first commission.
path.objective: Choose a buying niche and one platform, join affiliate programs, publish your first honest review by Day 10, keep posting on a schedule with clear disclosures, track your link clicks and finish with real numbers and a plan for the next 30 days.
path.typicalPrice: Commissions are usually a few percent of each sale, so volume and trust matter
firstTasks: Pick a niche where people already research and buy products
Choose one platform you can publish on every week
Apply to two or three affiliate programs and read their terms
Publish your first honest, disclosed review by Day 10
workflow: Pick a niche where people research products before they buy
Choose one platform and set up a simple home base
Join affiliate programs that fit and read each one's rules
Find what buyers search for: reviews, comparisons and "best X for Y"
Publish honest content with clear disclosures near every link
Track clicks and commissions for each post
Improve the posts that get clicks and grow an email list or following

tools.name: Google Trends
tools.purpose: Compare interest in product topics and spot seasonal buying

tools.name: Google Search autocomplete
tools.purpose: Collect the exact phrases people type before they buy

tools.name: Publishing platform
tools.purpose: Pick one, such as a free blog, Pinterest, YouTube, TikTok or a newsletter tool, to publish on

tools.name: Google Sheets
tools.purpose: Track programs, posts, link clicks and commissions in one place

tools.name: Canva
tools.purpose: Make pins, thumbnails and simple comparison graphics

tools.name: Email tool
tools.purpose: Start a small list on the free plan of a tool such as MailerLite, Kit or Beehiiv

plan.missionTitle: Pick a niche where people research products before they buy.
plan.goal: Write one sentence about who you help and the kind of products they buy.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 1 lesson
tasks.description: See how affiliate content works: you help people choose, they buy through your disclosed link, and the store pays you a small commission.

tasks.title: Name your audience
tasks.description: Write who you want to help in plain words, such as "new runners" or "people setting up a home office".

tasks.title: List what they buy
tasks.description: Write ten products or tools that audience buys, from small items to bigger purchases.

tasks.title: Write your niche sentence
tasks.description: Use this shape: "I help [audience] choose [type of products] for [goal]." Keep it to one sentence.

tasks.title: Set your 30-day goal
tasks.description: Choose a goal you control, such as "publish eight honest posts with disclosed links". Commissions are not fully in your control yet.

plan.nicheHint: Start from this draft: I help {audience} choose products for {problem}. Then circle the three products in your list that {audience} research the most before buying.

stageHints.idea: Pick a niche you already spend money and time on, so you can speak from real use.
stageHints.started: Look at the content you already posted and write the niche it is really about.
stageHints.some_traction: Write your niche sentence around the products that already earned you a commission.
stageHints.already_earning: List which product categories earn the most for you; this month builds on them.

plan.missionTitle: Confirm that people in your niche actively look for buying advice.
plan.goal: Collect 15 real buying questions people ask about your niche.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 2 lesson
tasks.description: Learn the difference between topics people read for fun and topics people research before spending money.

tasks.title: Search for buying questions
tasks.description: Type your product types into Google, YouTube and Reddit and copy questions like "which is better" or "is it worth it".

tasks.title: Check that reviews exist
tasks.description: If other people already publish reviews and comparisons on these products, buyers are looking. That is a good sign.

tasks.title: Note price ranges
tasks.description: Write the rough price of each product. Very cheap items earn tiny commissions, so mix in some mid-priced products.

tasks.title: Decide go or adjust
tasks.description: If people ask buying questions often and products exist at several price points, keep the niche. If not, narrow or shift it.

plan.nicheHint: Search for {terms} plus words like "best", "review" and "vs". Note how {audience} describe {problem} in their own words before buying.

stageHints.idea: Do not fall in love with the niche yet; let the questions you find decide.
stageHints.started: Check whether the topics you already post about have buying questions attached to them.
stageHints.some_traction: Look for buying questions close to the products that already convert for you.
stageHints.already_earning: Find buying questions in a neighbouring product category you have not covered yet.

plan.missionTitle: Choose the single platform you will publish on for the next 30 days.
plan.goal: Pick one platform and write why it fits you and your niche.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 3 lesson
tasks.description: Compare blogs, Pinterest, short videos, YouTube and newsletters for affiliate content, including how each one handles links.

tasks.title: Compare the five options
tasks.description: Blog: slow to start, strong with search. Pinterest: visual, link-friendly. Short videos: fast reach, links in bio. YouTube: long shelf life. Newsletter: direct trust.

tasks.title: Match it to your strengths
tasks.description: Pick the format you can produce every week without dread: writing, photos, talking on camera or emails.

tasks.title: Check link rules
tasks.description: Read how your chosen platform allows links and affiliate content. Some restrict links in posts or require a disclosure setting.

tasks.title: Commit for 30 days
tasks.description: Write your choice and one sentence on why. Other platforms can wait until this one works.

plan.nicheHint: Ask where {audience} go when they research {problem}. If they search Google, a blog fits; if they browse ideas, Pinterest; if they watch demos, video.

stageHints.idea: Choose the format you would enjoy making even if no one watched for a month.
stageHints.started: Stay on the platform you already use unless it clearly blocks the links you need.
stageHints.some_traction: Keep the platform that sent your first commissions as your main one.
stageHints.already_earning: Keep your main platform and note one secondary platform to test later, not now.

plan.missionTitle: Create or tidy the profile, blog or newsletter where your content will live.
plan.goal: Have a clear home base with a bio that says who you help.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 4 lesson
tasks.description: Set up a simple, trustworthy home base with free tools: a clear name, a plain bio and an about section.

tasks.title: Create or open your account
tasks.description: Use the free version of your platform. A paid theme or tool is not needed to start.

tasks.title: Write a clear bio
tasks.description: Say who you help and what you review, for example "Honest gear reviews for new runners".

tasks.title: Add an about section
tasks.description: Explain why you care about this niche and how you test or research products.

tasks.title: Add a disclosure note
tasks.description: Add a short line that you may earn a commission from links. You will refine it on Day 7.

plan.nicheHint: Write your bio for one person from {audience} who is stuck on {problem}. They should know within five seconds that your content is for them.

stageHints.idea: Keep it simple; a clear bio beats a perfect design.
stageHints.started: Rewrite your bio so it names your audience and what you review.
stageHints.some_traction: Make sure your about section explains how you choose what to recommend.
stageHints.already_earning: Check that your bio and about page still match the products you now cover.

plan.missionTitle: Find the affiliate programs that fit the products you want to recommend.
plan.goal: List at least six programs with their commission and cookie details.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 5 lesson
tasks.description: Learn the three main sources of programs: big retailers like Amazon Associates, brand programs, and networks like Impact or ShareASale.

tasks.title: Check the big retailers
tasks.description: Look up Amazon Associates and other large stores your audience buys from. Note their rules and payment thresholds.

tasks.title: Look for brand programs
tasks.description: Search "[brand] affiliate program" for products you use. Many brands run their own or list on a network.

tasks.title: Browse a network
tasks.description: Create a free publisher account on a network such as Impact, ShareASale or Awin only if it fits, and search your niche.

tasks.title: Record the details
tasks.description: For each program note commission rate, cookie length, approval rules and payout minimum. Approval rules vary by program.

plan.nicheHint: Search "{terms} affiliate program" and list brands {audience} already trust for {problem}. Prefer programs for products you have used or researched.

stageHints.idea: Some programs want existing content before they approve you, so list easy-to-join ones too.
stageHints.started: Look for programs matching products you already mentioned in past posts.
stageHints.some_traction: Check whether a brand program pays more than the retailer you use now.
stageHints.already_earning: Compare your current programs' terms and look for one better-fitting brand program.

plan.missionTitle: Apply to two or three programs and understand their rules.
plan.goal: Submit your applications and write down each program's key rules.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 6 lesson
tasks.description: Affiliate terms decide where you may post links, what you may say and when you get paid. Learn what to look for.

tasks.title: Apply to two or three programs
tasks.description: Fill in each application honestly, describing your platform and audience as they are today.

tasks.title: Read the terms
tasks.description: Look for rules on where links may appear, prices in posts, email use, paid ads and account closure.

tasks.title: Note deadlines
tasks.description: Some programs close accounts without qualifying sales in a set time. Write any deadline you find in your sheet.

tasks.title: Plan for a rejection
tasks.description: If a program says no, note why and reapply after you have published more content.

plan.nicheHint: Write down any program rules that matter for {problem}-related products, such as restrictions on health claims or price mentions.

stageHints.idea: It is normal to be declined at first; publishing a few posts often helps on the second try.
stageHints.started: Include links to your existing posts in your applications.
stageHints.some_traction: Ask your best-performing brand whether they have a higher tier or better terms.
stageHints.already_earning: Re-read the terms of your main program; rules change and old posts may need updates.

plan.missionTitle: Make clear disclosure part of everything you publish.
plan.goal: Write your standard disclosure lines and turn on any platform disclosure settings.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 7 lesson
tasks.description: Always tell people when you may earn from a link, clearly and close to the link, the way FTC-style guidance expects, and follow each platform's own rules.

tasks.title: Read the checklist
tasks.description: Go through the disclosure checklist and note what applies to your platform.

tasks.title: Write your disclosure lines
tasks.description: Write a short line for posts, such as "I may earn a commission if you buy through these links, at no extra cost to you."

tasks.title: Place it near the link
tasks.description: Put the disclosure before or right next to the first link, not hidden at the bottom or behind a click.

tasks.title: Turn on platform settings
tasks.description: Use the platform's paid partnership or affiliate label where it exists, in addition to your own words.

plan.nicheHint: If {problem} touches health or money for {audience}, also add a line that your content is educational and not medical or financial advice.

stageHints.idea: Build the habit now so every post starts with disclosure built in.
stageHints.started: Go back through any posts with links and add a clear disclosure near each one.
stageHints.some_traction: Check that disclosures show on mobile and in short-video captions, not only on desktop.
stageHints.already_earning: Audit your top posts for disclosure placement; earning more means more people are reading them.

plan.missionTitle: Find what people search for right before they buy in your niche.
plan.goal: List 20 search ideas grouped into reviews, comparisons, "best X for Y" and how-tos.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 8 lesson
tasks.description: Learn the four kinds of buyer searches and why they convert better than general information searches.

tasks.title: Use autocomplete
tasks.description: Type each product into Google, YouTube or Pinterest search and copy the suggestions that appear.

tasks.title: Group your ideas
tasks.description: Sort them into reviews, comparisons ("X vs Y"), "best X for Y" and how-tos.

tasks.title: Check what ranks
tasks.description: Open the top results for three ideas and note what they cover and what they miss.

tasks.title: Pick your first three
tasks.description: Choose three ideas you can answer honestly from use or solid research.

plan.nicheHint: Combine {terms} with "best", "vs", "review" and "for beginners" and note which phrases match the way {audience} talk about {problem}.

stageHints.idea: Favour specific searches, such as "best budget X for beginners", over broad ones.
stageHints.started: Check which of your existing posts already match a buyer search, and which do not.
stageHints.some_traction: Look for searches related to the post that earned your commission.
stageHints.already_earning: Find comparison searches for the products you already sell well.

plan.missionTitle: Choose the product for your first honest review and outline it.
plan.goal: Finish an outline for one review using the template.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 9 lesson
tasks.description: A good review answers who the product is for, who it is not for, and what it is really like to use.

tasks.title: Pick the product
tasks.description: Choose something you own and have used. If you do not own it yet, plan a research-based post and say so clearly.

tasks.title: Fill in the template
tasks.description: Outline: who it is for, what you tested, pros, cons, who should skip it and alternatives.

tasks.title: Gather proof
tasks.description: Take your own photos, screenshots or short clips. Avoid copying brand images unless the program allows it.

tasks.title: Note your honest verdict
tasks.description: Write one sentence on whether you would buy it again and why.

plan.nicheHint: Write the review for someone from {audience} trying to solve {problem}. Say clearly who the product suits and who should pick something else.

stageHints.idea: Review something you already own; your real experience is your advantage.
stageHints.started: Turn a product you mentioned in passing into a full, honest review.
stageHints.some_traction: Review a product your readers asked about in comments or messages.
stageHints.already_earning: Review the main alternative to your best-selling recommendation.

plan.missionTitle: Write or film your first review and publish it with a clear disclosure.
plan.goal: Publish one honest review with disclosed affiliate links.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 10 lesson
tasks.description: Version 1 is about published, not perfect. Learn how to finish, check and publish your first review.

tasks.title: Draft or film it
tasks.description: Follow your outline. Use short sentences, real details and at least one honest con.

tasks.title: Add your links
tasks.description: Add your affiliate link where readers naturally need it, not in every sentence.

tasks.title: Check the disclosure
tasks.description: Confirm the disclosure sits near the first link and is easy to read on a phone.

tasks.title: Publish it
tasks.description: Publish today, even if you would like to polish more. You can update it later.

plan.nicheHint: Read your review as someone from {audience} who has never heard of you. Does it help with {problem} even if they never click a link?

stageHints.idea: Your first post will not be your best, and that is fine; publishing is the win today.
stageHints.started: If you have posts without links, publish this one with links and a disclosure done right.
stageHints.some_traction: Use the format of your best-performing post for this review.
stageHints.already_earning: Publish a review that fills a gap in your existing content.

plan.missionTitle: Choose a realistic weekly publishing rhythm and plan the next two weeks.
plan.goal: Fill in a two-week posting schedule you can actually keep.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 11 lesson
tasks.description: Consistency builds both trust and search visibility. Learn to pick a rhythm you can keep for months.

tasks.title: Choose your rhythm
tasks.description: Pick a number you can sustain, such as two blog posts, five pins or three short videos a week.

tasks.title: Block the time
tasks.description: Put fixed creation slots in your calendar, like any other appointment.

tasks.title: Fill two weeks
tasks.description: Assign one search idea to each slot from your Day 8 list.

tasks.title: Plan a backup
tasks.description: Write one easy post idea you can use on a busy day so the schedule does not break.

plan.nicheHint: Plan posts that each solve one small part of {problem} for {audience}, using {terms} in your titles.

stageHints.idea: Start smaller than you think; you can always add more later.
stageHints.started: Make your schedule match what you already manage, then add one post a week.
stageHints.some_traction: Schedule more of the format that earned your commission.
stageHints.already_earning: Plan posts around your best sellers' seasons and buying moments.

plan.missionTitle: Draft a fair comparison of two or three products people choose between.
plan.goal: Finish a comparison draft with a clear recommendation for each type of buyer.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 12 lesson
tasks.description: Comparisons help buyers who are already close to a decision. Learn how to compare fairly without forcing a winner.

tasks.title: Pick the matchup
tasks.description: Choose two or three products people often compare, using a "vs" search from your list.

tasks.title: Build the table
tasks.description: Compare the same points for each: price range, key features, best for, main drawback.

tasks.title: Recommend by buyer type
tasks.description: Say which product suits which person instead of declaring one winner for everyone.

tasks.title: Be open about your sources
tasks.description: Say which products you used and which you researched from specs and owner reviews.

plan.nicheHint: Compare products {audience} actually choose between for {problem}, and match each one to a different kind of buyer.

stageHints.idea: Compare products in one price range so the comparison is fair.
stageHints.started: Turn two of your existing mentions into one clear comparison.
stageHints.some_traction: Compare the product that converted against its closest alternative.
stageHints.already_earning: Update or create a comparison for your highest-earning category.

plan.missionTitle: Finish and publish your comparison, then share it in allowed places.
plan.goal: Publish your comparison with disclosures and share it where self-promotion is welcome.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 13 lesson
tasks.description: Learn how to share content without spamming: use your own channels and follow each community's rules.

tasks.title: Final check
tasks.description: Check prices are described as approximate, links work and the disclosure is near the first link.

tasks.title: Publish it
tasks.description: Publish on your main platform today.

tasks.title: Share on your own channels
tasks.description: Share the post on your own profile, list or page. Do not drop links in other people's comments or groups.

tasks.title: Help where it is allowed
tasks.description: If a community allows it, answer a question fully first and only link when it is welcome and permitted.

plan.nicheHint: Write a short intro for the post that speaks to {audience} who are stuck choosing between options for {problem}.

stageHints.idea: Sharing on your own profile is enough for now; growth comes from consistency.
stageHints.started: Link this comparison from your earlier related posts.
stageHints.some_traction: Add this comparison to the post that already gets clicks.
stageHints.already_earning: Mention the new comparison to your email list or followers.

plan.missionTitle: Review what you published and fix anything that is missing.
plan.goal: Check every post for links, disclosures and clear next steps.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 14 lesson
tasks.description: Two weeks in, a short review keeps small mistakes from piling up. Learn what to check.

tasks.title: List what you published
tasks.description: Write every post with its date, platform and the products linked.

tasks.title: Audit disclosures
tasks.description: Open each post on your phone and confirm the disclosure is clear and near the links.

tasks.title: Check program status
tasks.description: See which applications were approved and swap links if a program declined you.

tasks.title: Adjust the schedule
tasks.description: If you missed slots, make the schedule smaller rather than giving up.

plan.nicheHint: Ask whether each post clearly helps {audience} with {problem}. Rewrite any intro that talks about the product before the reader's problem.

stageHints.idea: If you published one post, that is real progress. Plan the next one now.
stageHints.started: Count posts with links and disclosures done right; that is your true starting number.
stageHints.some_traction: Note which week 2 post has the most early views.
stageHints.already_earning: Compare this fortnight's output with your usual pace.

plan.missionTitle: Make your content more trustworthy with real use, pros and cons.
plan.goal: Update one post with honest cons, real photos and who should skip the product.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 15 lesson
tasks.description: Trust is the reason people buy through your link. Learn the habits that build it and the shortcuts that destroy it.

tasks.title: Run the trust checklist
tasks.description: Go through the checklist against your first review.

tasks.title: Add real proof
tasks.description: Add your own photos, measurements or screen recordings of the product in use.

tasks.title: Add honest cons
tasks.description: Write at least two real downsides and who should not buy it.

tasks.title: Set your rule
tasks.description: Write it down: "I only recommend things I would buy or have researched carefully." Never post fake or paid-for reviews.

plan.nicheHint: Tell {audience} exactly what you tested for {problem} and what you did not test. Being open about limits builds more trust than claiming everything.

stageHints.idea: Being honest about a product's flaws is the fastest way to stand out.
stageHints.started: Add cons and "who should skip it" to every review you already published.
stageHints.some_traction: Ask readers who bought what they think, and add their experience with permission.
stageHints.already_earning: Remove or update recommendations you would no longer buy yourself.

plan.missionTitle: Set up a simple way to see which posts get clicks and commissions.
plan.goal: Create a tracking sheet and tag links so you can tell posts apart.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 16 lesson
tasks.description: Learn how tracking IDs, sub-IDs and platform analytics show which posts send clicks, without paid tools.

tasks.title: Open the tracking sheet
tasks.description: Copy the link tracking sheet and add every post you have published.

tasks.title: Tag your links
tasks.description: Use your program's tracking ID or sub-ID feature so each post or platform gets its own tag where allowed.

tasks.title: Find your dashboards
tasks.description: Locate the clicks and earnings report in each program and your platform's analytics.

tasks.title: Set a weekly check
tasks.description: Pick one day a week to copy clicks and commissions into the sheet.

plan.nicheHint: Track which posts for {audience} get clicks, and note the {problem} angle each one used so you can spot patterns later.

stageHints.idea: Zero clicks so far is normal; the sheet is ready for when they come.
stageHints.started: Fill in past posts too so you can compare old and new.
stageHints.some_traction: Note which post and which product each commission came from.
stageHints.already_earning: Add earnings per click to see which posts are worth updating first.

plan.theme: Plan a "Best X for Y" Post
plan.missionTitle: Outline a "best X for Y" post for a specific type of buyer.
plan.goal: Finish an outline with 3 to 5 picks and a clear reason for each.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 17 lesson
tasks.description: "Best X for Y" posts match how many people search before buying. Learn to make them specific and honest.

tasks.title: Choose the Y
tasks.description: Pick a specific buyer or situation, such as "for small apartments" or "for beginners on a budget".

tasks.title: Pick 3 to 5 products
tasks.description: Choose products that really fit that buyer. Mark which you used and which you researched.

tasks.title: Write the criteria
tasks.description: List what matters most for that buyer and judge each pick against it.

tasks.title: Add a skip section
tasks.description: Note products you left out and why. It shows readers you did the work.

plan.nicheHint: Make the Y about {audience} and {problem}, for example "best {terms} for {audience}".

stageHints.idea: A narrow Y is easier to rank for and easier to write honestly.
stageHints.started: Build this post from products you already reviewed.
stageHints.some_traction: Include the product that earned a commission if it truly fits the buyer.
stageHints.already_earning: Target a Y your best posts do not cover yet.

plan.missionTitle: Write and publish your "best X for Y" post.
plan.goal: Publish the post with a short summary at the top and disclosures near links.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 18 lesson
tasks.description: Learn how to structure a list post so busy readers find the right pick fast.

tasks.title: Add a quick summary
tasks.description: Start with a short list of picks and who each one is for.

tasks.title: Write each pick
tasks.description: For each: why it is on the list, one pro, one con and who should choose it.

tasks.title: Disclose and link
tasks.description: Add your disclosure near the top before the first link, then link each pick once or twice.

tasks.title: Publish and log it
tasks.description: Publish and add it to your tracking sheet with its own link tag.

plan.nicheHint: Open by naming the situation {audience} are in with {problem}, then give your quick picks.

stageHints.idea: Done and helpful beats long and unfinished.
stageHints.started: Link to this post from your earlier reviews of the same products.
stageHints.some_traction: Place your strongest, most honest pick first.
stageHints.already_earning: Link this post from your best performer to pass on readers.

plan.missionTitle: Create a how-to post that solves a problem and mentions tools naturally.
plan.goal: Publish one helpful how-to that would be useful even without links.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 19 lesson
tasks.description: How-to content builds trust and reach. Learn to mention products only where they genuinely help.

tasks.title: Pick a question
tasks.description: Choose a how-to question from your Day 8 list or from comments.

tasks.title: Solve it fully
tasks.description: Write or film the full answer, step by step, including free options.

tasks.title: Mention tools where they help
tasks.description: Link a product only where a reader would naturally need it, with a disclosure nearby.

tasks.title: Publish and log it
tasks.description: Publish and add it to your tracking sheet.

plan.nicheHint: Answer a how-to question {audience} ask about {problem}. Include a free or no-purchase option so the post helps everyone.

stageHints.idea: How-tos are a gentle way to build an audience before you have many reviews.
stageHints.started: Turn a common question from your comments into a full post.
stageHints.some_traction: Write a how-to that leads naturally to the product that converts.
stageHints.already_earning: Create a how-to for buyers who already own your top product.

plan.theme: Start an Email List or Following
plan.missionTitle: Set up a simple way for readers to come back.
plan.goal: Create a free email signup or a clear follow call to action.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 20 lesson
tasks.description: Platforms change, but readers who choose to hear from you stay. Learn the simplest way to start a list.

tasks.title: Pick the tool
tasks.description: Use the free plan of an email tool, or your platform's own follow or subscribe feature.

tasks.title: Create a small freebie
tasks.description: Offer something useful, such as a buying checklist or a comparison cheat sheet.

tasks.title: Add the signup
tasks.description: Put the signup or follow call to action at the end of your best posts.

tasks.title: Write a welcome message
tasks.description: Say who you are, what you will send and how often. Include your disclosure policy.

plan.nicheHint: Make the freebie a short buying checklist for {audience} dealing with {problem}.

stageHints.idea: Even five subscribers is a start; they are people who chose to hear from you.
stageHints.started: Add a signup to every post you already published.
stageHints.some_traction: Put the signup on the post that earned a commission.
stageHints.already_earning: Write a welcome series that links your most helpful posts.

plan.missionTitle: Read your numbers and choose what to improve.
plan.goal: Fill in your tracking sheet and pick one post to improve next week.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 21 lesson
tasks.description: Learn to read views, clicks and commissions without overreacting to small numbers.

tasks.title: Update the sheet
tasks.description: Copy views, clicks and any commissions for every post.

tasks.title: Find the leader
tasks.description: Note which post has the most clicks, even if the number is small.

tasks.title: Spot the gap
tasks.description: Find posts with views but no clicks; they are your best fix candidates.

tasks.title: Pick one to improve
tasks.description: Choose one post to work on next week and write what you will change.

plan.nicheHint: Note which {problem} angle earned the most interest from {audience}. That is your best guess for what to make more of.

stageHints.idea: Small numbers are normal in week 3; look for any signal, not big results.
stageHints.started: Compare clicks on posts with links done right against older posts.
stageHints.some_traction: Calculate roughly how many clicks it took to earn one commission.
stageHints.already_earning: Compare this month's clicks per post with last month's.

plan.missionTitle: Make your best-clicked post even more useful.
plan.goal: Update your top post with clearer picks, fresh details and a better call to action.

tasks.title: Watch the Day 22 lesson
tasks.description: The fastest growth often comes from improving what already works. Learn what to update first.

tasks.title: Open your top post
tasks.description: Pick the post with the most clicks in your sheet.

tasks.title: Make the answer clearer
tasks.description: Add a quick summary, a comparison table or a clearer verdict near the top.

tasks.title: Refresh the details
tasks.description: Check that products are still available and descriptions are current.

tasks.title: Improve the call to action
tasks.description: Make the link text say what happens, such as "Check current price", with the disclosure still nearby.

plan.nicheHint: Re-read your top post as someone from {audience} in a hurry to solve {problem}. Make the answer visible within ten seconds.

stageHints.idea: If no post has clicks yet, improve the one with the most views.
stageHints.started: Improve the post that got your first clicks.
stageHints.some_traction: Improve the post that earned a commission first.
stageHints.already_earning: Update your top three earners, starting with the oldest.

plan.missionTitle: Find out why a post with readers is not getting clicks.

text.affiliate_content:
The best first products to promote are ones you already use or know well, in a niche where people research before buying.

1. List ten products you own and use in your niche.
2. Search each one with "review" or "vs" and see if people ask about it.
3. Pick the two or three where you have a real, honest opinion.

Next step: write one sentence on why you would recommend each pick, and to whom.

followUps: How do I find programs for these products?
Can I review something I do not own?
What should my first post be?

text.affiliate_content:
Start with two or three programs that cover products you would honestly recommend.

1. Check big retailers your audience buys from, such as Amazon Associates.
2. Search "[brand] affiliate program" for brands you use.
3. Look at networks such as Impact or ShareASale for more brands.

Approval rules vary, and some programs want existing content first. If you are declined, publish a few posts and reapply.

Next step: fill in the Affiliate Program Finder for six programs.

followUps: What should I check in the terms?
Amazon or brand programs?
What if I get rejected?

text.affiliate_content:
Always tell people when you may earn from a link. Make it clear, plain and close to the link.

1. Use simple words: "I may earn a commission if you buy through these links."
2. Put it before or right next to the first link, not hidden at the bottom.
3. Turn on your platform's paid partnership or affiliate label where it exists, and follow each program's wording rules.

This is general guidance, not legal advice, and rules differ by country.

Next step: open the Disclosure Checklist and check your latest post.

followUps: Where do I put it in a video?
Do I disclose in emails too?
What about health products?

text.affiliate_content:
No clicks in the first weeks is very common. Affiliate content usually takes time to be found.

1. Check your posts answer buyer searches like reviews, comparisons or "best X for Y".
2. Make sure links appear where readers make a decision, with clear link text.
3. Keep publishing on schedule; each post is another way to be found.

Next step: pick your most-viewed post and add a short "which one should I pick" section.

followUps: How do I get more traffic?
Where should links go?
How long does this usually take?

text.affiliate_content:
Clicks without sales usually mean the reader was not ready to buy, or the product was not the right fit.

1. Check whether the post matches buying intent or just curiosity.
2. Make sure you recommend the right product for the right buyer, with honest cons.
3. Check your links go to the exact product and that it is in stock.

Commissions can lag behind clicks, so give it a few weeks before changing everything.

Next step: open your tracking sheet and compare clicks on your top three posts.

followUps: How do I improve a post?
Should I change programs?
How do I build more trust?

text.affiliate_content:
Pick the one platform you can publish on every week for months.

1. Blog: slower to start, strong with search.
2. Pinterest: visual and link-friendly.
3. Short videos: fast reach, usually links in bio.
4. YouTube: long shelf life for reviews.
5. Newsletter: direct trust with readers.

Check each platform's link and affiliate rules before choosing.

Next step: choose one and commit to it for 30 days.

text.affiliate_content:
Both can work, and many people use a mix.

1. Big retailers like Amazon are familiar to buyers and cover many products, but rates are often low and cookies short.
2. Brand programs may pay more per sale and offer longer cookies, but cover fewer products.
3. Rules differ, so read each one's terms before linking.

Next step: for your top three products, compare the retailer and brand program terms in your finder sheet.

text.affiliate_content:
Honesty is what makes people trust your links.

1. Only recommend things you would buy or have researched carefully.
2. Always include real cons and who should skip the product.
3. If a product disappoints you or readers report problems, update the post and say what changed.

If buyers return a product, the commission on it may be reversed. That is one more reason to recommend only what fits.

Next step: add two honest cons to your latest review.

text.affiliate_content:
You can write about products you have not used, as long as you are transparent and do the research.

1. Say clearly that you have not used it yourself.
2. Lean on specs, manuals, official information and patterns in many owner reviews.
3. Compare it with products you have used, if you can.

Never pretend you tested something you did not. A research-based comparison can still be very helpful.

Next step: write a comparison that mixes one product you own with two you researched.

text.affiliate_content:
Traffic for affiliate content mostly comes from being found when people search, plus steady posting.

1. Build posts around buyer searches from autocomplete.
2. Use clear titles with the words people type.
3. Publish on a steady schedule and update posts that already get views.

Share on your own channels, but never drop links in other people's comments or groups.

Next step: add five new ideas to your Search Ideas Worksheet.

text.affiliate_content:
An email list keeps readers even when platforms change.

1. Start with the free plan of an email tool or your platform's subscribe feature.
2. Offer a small freebie, such as a buying checklist.
3. Send helpful emails first, then link to posts, and disclose any affiliate links.

Check that each program allows links in email before including them.

Next step: open the Email List Starter and pick a freebie idea.

text.affiliate_content:
Affiliate income usually grows slowly, so feeling tired or stuck is common.

1. Shrink your schedule to the smallest output that still counts.
2. Batch research, writing and publishing into separate sessions.
3. Count what you built: posts, programs and updates, not only income.

Next step: write your weekly minimum, such as one post and one update, and protect that time.

text.affiliate_content:
Dropping links in comments, groups or DMs usually gets them removed and can break program and platform rules.

1. Share on your own profile, blog, list or page.
2. In communities, answer questions fully and only link when it is welcome and allowed.
3. Never ask people to click as a favour or trade clicks.

Next step: reply helpfully to one question in your niche without a link.

text.affiliate_content:
Good question. Tell me a bit more so I can be specific: your niche, which platform you use and what you are trying to improve.

Until then, the rule that fixes most early affiliate problems is simple: publish one more honest, helpful post with a clear disclosure. Steady publishing teaches more than a week of planning.
